title: Casal de idosos do sertão descobre água em poço e comemora feito criança o fim da seca; vídeo
content:
Casal de idosos do sertão descobre água em poço e comemora feito criança o fim da seca; vídeo
A felicidade deles é contagiante. Esse casal de idosos, que viveu anos na seca no sertão, encontra água em poço profundo em casa e comemora feito criança. Assim que o jato começa a sair com força do solo, os dois se aproximam, se molham e um deles chega a se ajoelhar no chão.
O vídeo foi compartilhado pela influenciadora Rayane Vieira Inácio, de Baturité, no Ceará, no perfil @rayane_vieira09. “Só quem é nordestino vai entender”, escreveu ela na publicação.
Nas imagens, o casal sorri e brinca com a água que jorra do poço. Em determinado momento, o homem chega a se deitar próximo ao local para receber o jato e a mulher também entra na água. Uma verdadeira festa!
Descoberta virou banho de comemoração
O vídeo em que o casal de idosos encontra água em poço chamou atenção pela reação espontânea dos dois, que transformaram a descoberta em um banho de comemoração.
A chegada de água pode fazer diferença para famílias que vivem em áreas rurais atingidas pela estiagem, onde o abastecimento costuma ser um desafio durante vários meses do ano.
Além do consumo doméstico, poços podem ajudar no abastecimento de animais e em outras atividades da rotina no campo, dependendo da qualidade e da disponibilidade da água encontrada.

Rayane Vieira, que publicou o registro, é influenciadora e mora em Baturité, no interior do Ceará. Ela já ficou conhecida nas redes por mostrar cenas da rotina na região.
Apesar da origem da publicação, não há confirmação de que o vídeo tenha sido gravado em Baturité. A postagem também não informa os nomes do casal nem a cidade e o estado onde fica o poço.

title: Giải phóng xong mặt bằng đường nối Phạm Hùng - Lê Đức Thọ, Hà Nội trước ngày 30-9
content:
Dự án đường nối Phạm Hùng - Lê Đức Thọ, phường Từ Liêm, Hà Nội dài 1,12km đang được đẩy nhanh công tác giải phóng mặt bằng, phấn đấu hoàn thành trước ngày 30-9-2026.
Ghi nhận của Tuổi Trẻ, sau gần 10 năm vướng giải phóng mặt bằng, hiện nhiều hộ dân trong phạm vi dự án đường nối Phạm Hùng - Lê Đức Thọ, phường Từ Liêm, Hà Nội đang khẩn trương dời nhà, bàn giao mặt bằng để thi công tuyến đường.
Bà Nguyễn Thị Sáu, ngõ 252 Mỹ Đình, cho biết gia đình bà gắn bó với ngôi nhà này từ năm 1992. Căn nhà có diện tích hơn 300m2, nhưng sau khi giải phóng mặt bằng chỉ còn lại hơn 60m2.
"Tâm trạng tôi lúc này vui buồn đan xen. Vui vì sau này nhà mình ra mặt đường, đường trước nhà to đẹp. Nhưng buồn vì ngôi nhà gắn bó với gia đình từ nhiều năm, lưu giữ rất nhiều kỷ niệm, giờ chỉ còn hơn 60m2", bà Sáu chia sẻ.
Trao đổi với Tuổi Trẻ, ông Lê Quang Hợp - Giám đốc Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư - hạ tầng phường Từ Liêm - cho biết theo kế hoạch, công tác giải phóng mặt bằng hoàn thành trước 30-9, nhưng thực tế đang được đẩy nhanh hơn so với mốc kế hoạch ban đầu.
Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư - hạ tầng cũng đã làm việc với các nhà thầu để chuẩn bị tiếp nhận mặt bằng, tổ chức dọn dẹp và triển khai thi công, đảm bảo an toàn lao động và giao thông trong khu vực.
"Đến hiện tại 95% bà con có tinh thần ủng hộ rất cao, chỉ có một số trường hợp UBND phường đang tiếp tục vận động để đạt kết quả giải phóng mặt bằng cao nhất. Chúng tôi đang mời các nhà thầu, ngay ngày mai các nhà thầu có thể tiến hành giao nhận mặt bằng, dọn dẹp để đảm bảo vệ sinh môi trường, an toàn giao thông, lao động trên địa bàn", ông Hợp nói.
Việc đẩy nhanh giải phóng mặt bằng được xem là bước chuyển quan trọng để hoàn thành tuyến đường nối Phạm Hùng - Lê Đức Thọ đang còn dang dở - Ảnh: PHÚC TÀI
UBND phường Đông Ngạc (Hà Nội) cho biết hệ thống thoát nước tại khu vực nơi nam sinh viên năm nhất rơi xuống cống tử vong là do Trung tâm Quản lý hạ tầng kỹ thuật TP (Sở Xây dựng Hà Nội) quản lý.
Thêm chuyên mục, tăng trải nghiệm với Tuổi Trẻ Sao

title: Chinese experts revive Juba Hospital CT Scanner after 10 months
content:
A Chinese medical team has repaired and restored a Computed Tomography (CT) scanner at Juba Teaching Hospital after the machine remained out of service for about 10 months, hospital authorities said.
As the only CT scanner available at Juba Teaching Hospital, the machine suffered a sudden breakdown and ceased operation completely in November 2025.
Core‑hardware failures involving several detector modules were compounded by chewed‑and‑damaged critical optical‑fiber cables due to rampant rat infestations inside the hospital; the combination of multiple problems completely paralyzed the equipment.
For CT scans, residents had to turn to expensive private‑sector facilities, which were unaffordable for ordinary households.
Zhao Yao, Deputy Head of CT Scanner Operations, said the equipment suffered complex and extensive damage caused by multiple overlapping malfunctions.
“The problem is very complicated. One, because the power is not very stable. Power off, power on, it is very easy to get the machine broken down, out of work,” he explained. “Another very important problem is caused by the rats.”
Yao said he received remote technical guidance from senior engineers based in China while conducting on-site inspections, which enabled him to identify the problem and successfully repair the machine.
“We have just arrived here. Once we know the problem, our doctor and engineer communicate with the engineer in China,” he said. “Under the instruction of the Chinese engineer, our local engineer here cooperates, and we get the problem addressed.”
He said the equipment operated stably after being restarted and produced clear, standard-quality images, adding that 10 patients have so far undergone scans since the machine was restored.
This life‑saving piece of equipment is once again providing local people with accurate and efficient imaging diagnostic services, effectively alleviating the long‑standing medical‑access hardships faced by residents.
This successful repair of the machine by the 14th batch of the Chinese medical team has revived accurate large-scale imaging examinations at the hospital. Critically ill patients suffering from cerebral hemorrhage, cerebral infarction and other emergencies can now receive timely identification of underlying conditions, greatly improving treatment outcomes.
Lero Anna, a radiology technologist at Juba Teaching Hospital, noted that the CT scanner broke down due to persistent power outages and implored the hospital management to secure a stable emergency power supply to mitigate damage to the CT scanner.
“The CT scan machine was really helping, but then we had issues with the electricity. You could be scanning a patient, and then the electricity just goes off, which stops the machine from working,” she said. “Most times, the temperature of the machine would be really high, which affects how it works. So, usually we need it to cool down, and then we put it off.”
She said that since the repair, the facility now receives between eight and 10 patients per day for CT scans.
“The big issue is just with the electricity,” Anna said. “If that can be fixed, then the department will run well, and we will be able to help more patients because, on average, we help about 8 to 10 patients in a day.”

title: Cardiac rehabilitation cuts hospital admissions and heart attack risk
content:
Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation reduces hospital admissions by a third and heart attack risk by more than a quarter, as well as remaining beneficial in the long term, a new Cochrane review finds. The evidence also suggests that newer home-based and digitally supported cardiac rehabilitation programs can be just as effective as traditional center-based services. The work is published in Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews.
Coronary heart disease is the single most common cause of death globally. It can lead to chest pain, heart attacks or stroke. Cardiac rehabilitation programs are widely recommended following a cardiac event, with exercise recognized as a core component.
Effective and inexpensive intervention
The researchers, led by the University of Glasgow, analyzed 107 randomized controlled trials involving 26,886 people with coronary heart disease. Most participants had experienced a heart attack, undergone heart procedures or experienced some sort of chest pain. Women were underrepresented, making up only 17% of participants despite being included in most studies.
The overall results show that, compared with no program, exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation reduces heart attacks by 28%, reduces all-cause hospital admissions by 35% and probably reduces deaths.
Participants also reported better physical functioning, general health, vitality, social functioning and mental well-being. These benefits were seen across several validated quality-of-life measures.
"Our review shows that exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation can reduce the risk of heart attack and hospital admission while helping people return to healthier, more active lives," says Dr. Grace Dibben, lead author from the University of Glasgow.
"Many people lose confidence after a heart attack or cardiac procedure and worry that physical activity could be dangerous," Dibben adds. "Appropriately prescribed exercise is not only safe for most patients, but can play a vital role in recovery and long-term heart health."
Growing evidence for modern rehabilitation models
This new update included 22 new trials featuring just under 3,500 participants, incorporating more recent data into the final results. The more recent studies included participants based in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and tested home-based and digital cardiac rehabilitation programs.
"This review confirms that exercise is a great tool for improving the overall health of people with coronary heart disease," says Professor Rod Taylor, senior author from the University of Glasgow. "By adding newer studies to this update, we're able to see that digital programs work as well as in-person programs, which really changes the game here. These approaches may help us reach people who cannot attend traditional center-based services."
Several studies in this update were conducted in LMICs, examining different types of exercise in different countries; for example, yoga in India and tai chi in China. The authors suggest this not only improves the relevance of the evidence base, but that some populations may find rehabilitation built around traditional and cultural forms of exercise more appealing than conventional, machine-based rehab.
Low uptake despite evidence-backed benefits
Despite strong evidence supporting cardiac rehabilitation, uptake remains a challenge in many health care systems. Various guidelines, including NICE in the UK, recognize cardiac rehabilitation as a key component following a cardiac event. However, cardiac rehabilitation continues to be widely underused, with generally low participation rates. According to the 2025 National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation (NACR) report, the uptake of cardiac rehabilitation for patients with acute coronary syndrome was 44.5% in England and 71.3% in Wales.
The authors explain that many patients face barriers to attending traditional hospital-based programs, including work commitments, transportation challenges and caregiving responsibilities. This can disproportionately affect groups such as women, older adults and people in deprived communities.
"Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation is an inexpensive and cost-effective intervention, but right now it's underfunded and unprioritized," Dibben explains. "We want this option to be available to everyone. This new research shows you don't even have to go into a rehab center to benefit—you can participate from home and still see the benefits."

title: De plus en plus de Belges ont recours au temps partiel médical : "Les travailleurs ne retournent pas tous au travail"
content:
De plus en plus de Belges ont recours au temps partiel médical : "Les travailleurs ne retournent pas tous au travail"
Les personnes en incapacité de travail ont de plus en plus recours au temps partiel médical, a rapporté samedi L'Echo, sur la base de données récoltées auprès des mutuelles. Le dispositif mène dans un cas sur deux à une sortie complète de l'incapacité, a précisé le quotidien.
- Publié le 19-09-2026 à 07h32
- Mis à jour le 19-09-2026 à 14h06
Entre 2019 et mai 2026, la proportion de nouvelles reprises à temps partiel est passée de 9 à 15% chez les personnes en incapacité depuis moins d'un an et de 18,4 à 26,2% chez celles en incapacité de longue durée, ont indiqué les Mutualités libres. Et la Mutualité chrétienne, Solidaris et l'Inami observent la même évolution positive.
Depuis le début de 2026, les entreprises de plus de 20 travailleurs doivent évaluer, au moyen d'un questionnaire standardisé, le potentiel de retour au travail des personnes en incapacité depuis au moins huit semaines, afin de faciliter la reprise. Le service de prévention Cohezio estime qu'un contact direct est toutefois plus efficace.
Sur 6.700 demandes traitées depuis mars, le questionnaire a identifié un potentiel retour dans 15% des cas, contre 46% après un entretien téléphonique. Parmi les dossiers considérés comme négatifs sur la base du questionnaire, 52% se sont finalement avérés positifs après l'entretien.
Selon Cohezio, la différence s'explique par la nature même de l'échange. "Alors que le questionnaire mesure essentiellement la perception qu'a le travailleur de sa situation actuelle, l'entretien permet d'aborder les possibilités concrètes d'un retour au travail et d'explorer différents scénarios de reprise. Dans de nombreux cas, le dialogue aide les travailleurs à envisager des perspectives qu'ils n'avaient pas identifiées eux-mêmes."
Pour Evelyne Kerger, médecin et directrice générale chez Cohezio, "ces résultats ne montrent pas que les travailleurs retournent tous au travail. Ils montrent qu'il existe souvent davantage de possibilités qu'on ne le pense lorsqu'on prend le temps d'échanger avec eux sur leur situation et leurs perspectives".
La concrétisation d'un retour durable au travail dépend ensuite de nombreux facteurs, souligne le service de prévention: l'état de santé du travailleur, son projet professionnel, la capacité de l'employeur à adapter un poste ou à proposer une autre fonction, ainsi que la collaboration entre les différents acteurs impliqués dans le processus. "Le service de prévention, le médecin traitant, l'employeur, la ligne hiérarchique et le travailleur lui-même ont chacun également un rôle déterminant à jouer", selon Cohezio.

title: Tajikistan commissions new education and social facilities in Sughd region
content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 21. Tajikistan has commissioned new education, recreation and social infrastructure facilities in the Asht district of Sughd region.
According to the press service of the Tajik President, President Emomali Rahmon remotely commissioned the facilities on September 21 as part of his working visit to the district.
In particular, a new building for the Asht district education department was commissioned, providing working conditions for more than 50 employees.
The Bunyod LLC sanatorium also started operations in the Aksikon area of the Mehrobod rural jamoat. The facility has 120 beds and created 30 permanent jobs following its launch.
A preschool educational institution for 180 children was commissioned in the Dusti village. The facility was built at the initiative of local entrepreneur Rakhmonzoda Zoir Abdusamad. The launch of the kindergarten provided permanent employment for more than 20 local residents.
In addition, a State Flag Square was opened in the Shaydon settlement for public, cultural and other events.
An additional building of general education institution No. 9 in the Oriyon rural jamoat was also commissioned, with capacity for 240 students. The facility was financed by the executive authority of Sughd region.
Trend estimates that the newly commissioned education facilities could accommodate up to around 420 additional children and students, helping increase local educational capacity and reduce pressure on existing schools and kindergartens. If demand continues to rise, the additional capacity could support a gradual expansion of preschool and school enrollment in Asht district.
The new sanatorium could also contribute to the development of local recreational and health-related services. At an average occupancy rate of 60–70 percent, the facility could accommodate roughly 26,000–31,000 occupied bed-days annually, creating additional demand for transport, food, maintenance and other services connected with the local tourism and recreation economy.
Trend expects the expansion of education, healthcare and recreational infrastructure to support broader local economic activity over the next few years. If similar projects continue to be implemented, employment generated directly and indirectly by social facilities could increase by approximately 5–8 percent annually, while growing demand for related services could provide additional opportunities for local businesses. These figures are Trend estimates based on the capacity of the newly commissioned facilities and standard utilization assumptions, rather than an official forecast.

title: Corridas patrimoniales convierten las calles de Santiago de Chile en un museo al aire libre
content:
Corridas patrimoniales convierten las calles de Santiago de Chile en un museo al aire libre
Lectores Corresponsales
Cada mes, decenas de personas recorren distintos barrios de la capital chilena junto a un historiador, en una experiencia que combina actividad física y memoria urbana, invitando a un redescubrimiento de la ciudad
* El autor forma parte de la comunidad de lectores de La Vanguardia
Cada mes, decenas de personas recorren distintos barrios de la capital junto a un historiador, en una experiencia que combina actividad física, patrimonio y memoria urbana, invitando a redescubrir Santiago desde una perspectiva poco habitual.
Entre los principales hitos patrimoniales visitados destacan el Palacio Cousiño, el Palacio de La Moneda, el Club Hípico, la Escuela Militar, la Estación Mapocho, la Plaza Yungay, además de distintos edificios y espacios emblemáticos de barrios como el Cívico, El Golf, Barrio Italia, Yungay y, más recientemente, el Barrio Universitario
Las mismas calles por donde miles de santiaguinos corren cada semana también guardan historias de inmigración, arquitectura, educación, política y desarrollo urbano que muchas veces pasan inadvertidas. Hoy, una iniciativa busca cambiar esa mirada, convirtiendo cada recorrido en una oportunidad para descubrir el patrimonio de la ciudad mientras se practica deporte.
Cada mes, decenas de personas participan en recorridos guiados por distintos barrios de Santiago, acompañados por el historiador Cristóbal García-Huidobro, quien durante el trayecto comparte relatos, personajes y acontecimientos que marcaron la identidad de cada sector. Así, edificios, plazas, iglesias y espacios públicos dejan de ser parte del paisaje cotidiano para transformarse en escenarios donde la historia vuelve a cobrar vida.
Desde su creación, la iniciativa ha recorrido cerca de 30 kilómetros por distintos barrios de Santiago y ya ha convocado a alrededor de 500 participantes. El interés ha ido creciendo de manera sostenida y los cupos suelen agotarse en pocos minutos, reflejando una creciente búsqueda por panoramas que integren deporte, cultura y vida en comunidad.
Entre los principales hitos patrimoniales visitados destacan el Palacio Cousiño, el Palacio de La Moneda, el Club Hípico, la Escuela Militar, la Estación Mapocho, la Plaza Yungay, además de distintos edificios y espacios emblemáticos de barrios como el Cívico, El Golf, Barrio Italia, Yungay y, más recientemente, el Barrio Universitario. En cada recorrido, la historia se entrelaza con el ejercicio físico para ofrecer una experiencia distinta de conocer la ciudad.
Desde su creación, ha recorrido cerca de 30 km por distintos barrios de Santiago y ya ha convocado a alrededor de 500 participantes
La propuesta se inserta en una tendencia que busca recuperar el espacio público como un lugar de encuentro ciudadano y acercar el patrimonio a nuevas audiencias mediante experiencias participativas. En ese contexto, iniciativas que combinan actividad física con relatos históricos están abriendo nuevas formas de relacionarse con la ciudad, invitando a descubrir que la historia también puede encontrarse fuera de museos, libros o salas de clases.
Los recorridos son organizados por la comunidad Run Capital e impulsados junto a la marca deportiva chilena Vulcano, bajo el concepto de “Re-Correr la ciudad”. El sábado 29 de agosto, la corrida tuvo como escenario el tradicional barrio El Aguilucho, sumando un nuevo capítulo a esta forma distinta de explorar Santiago. Asimismo, la siguiente fecha es en el Barrio Bicentenario que se va a hacer el viernes 25 de septiembre y, la fecha 8, será en el Barrio Bellavista, cuya fecha pactada es el sábado 17 de octubre.
Para Maximiliano Walther, Brand Manager de Vulcano, este tipo de iniciativas reflejan cómo el deporte puede transformarse en una herramienta para fortalecer el vínculo de las personas con su entorno. “Cuando una corrida incorpora historia, patrimonio y espacios públicos, deja de ser solo una actividad deportiva y pasa a convertirse en una experiencia que invita a conocer mejor la ciudad y a valorar su identidad. Ese es el tipo de iniciativas que creemos vale la pena impulsar porque generan comunidad y promueven una forma distinta de habitar Santiago”, afirmó.
Más que completar una ruta, la invitación es a mirar la ciudad con otros ojos y comprender que detrás de cada calle, edificio o plaza existen historias que siguen construyendo la identidad de Santiago, demostrando que el deporte también puede convertirse en una puerta de entrada al patrimonio y la cultura urbana.

title: Farmers end indefinite stir in Kurugodu after officials assure water to D7 canal
content:
Farmers withdrew their overnight and indefinite protest near the Irrigation Department office in Kurugodu, Ballari district, on Saturday after officials assured them that water would be supplied to the tail-end areas of the D7 canal.
The protest, which had entered its second day, was launched by farmers demanding adequate water for irrigation as they prepare for sowing and to protect the standing crops. The farmers had insisted that at least 600 cusecs of water be released into the D7 canal until the onset of the next spell of rain.
An executive engineer from Ballari arrived at the protest site around 9 p.m. on Friday and held discussions with the farmers on the release of water. The talks initially failed to break the deadlock, with the farmers refusing to withdraw their agitation.
The farmers said they had lost confidence in assurances given by officials during an earlier protest on September 2, as the commitments made then had not been fulfilled. They demanded that the government immediately ensure the required quantity of water in the canal, particularly to enable water to reach villages and farms at the tail end of the system.
On Saturday, the assistant executive engineer of the taluk Irrigation Department held discussions with senior officials in the presence of departmental official Supreeth and assured the farmers that steps would be taken to ensure that water reached farmers in every village, including those at the tail end of the canal.
Following the assurance, the farmers called off their agitation.

title: Verein setzt auf frühe Sprachförderung
content:
„Je früher in die Sprachentwicklung investiert wird, desto weniger Probleme entstehen später“, sagt Lisa-Maria Sommer-Fein, Generalsekretärin der MEGA Bildungsstiftung gegenüber noe.ORF.at.
Genau hier setzt der Verein Startklar an. Seit 2018 hat die Initiative nach eigenen Angaben mehr als 8.500 Kinder in über 1.150 Sprachförderkursen erreicht. Mittlerweile ist Startklar an mehr als 80 Standorten in Niederösterreich, Wien und dem Burgenland vertreten. Das Angebot reicht von Deutschförder-Spielgruppen für Kindergartenkinder bis zu Kursen für Volks- und Mittelschulkinder. Auch Eltern sowie Pädagoginnen und Pädagogen werden einbezogen.
Sprache spielerisch vermitteln
Wie die Sprachförderung konkret aussieht, hängt vom jeweiligen Thema ab. Bei einer Einheit rund um Kleidung werden Taschen mit verschiedenen Kleidungsstücken mitgebracht, damit die Kinder zunächst die Begriffe kennenlernen. Gleichzeitig wird ein bestimmter grammatikalischer Schwerpunkt vermittelt. „Jede Einheit hat einen eigenen Sprachförderschwerpunkt“, erklärt Janine Fischer, geschäftsführende Obfrau und Leiterin von Startklar.
Auch die Leseförderung ist ein wichtiger Bestandteil der Arbeit, denn Lesen sei eine wichtige Basis für den weiteren Bildungsweg, betont Sommer-Fein. Bei Projekten wie „Lesen mit allen Sinnen“ werden Gegenstände aus den Geschichten mitgebracht und Handlungen gemeinsam nachgespielt. Eltern können ebenfalls teilnehmen und die Begeisterung für Bücher auch zu Hause weitergeben.
Lesen werde schon im frühkindlichen Alter zu Hause geprägt, sagt Sommer-Fein. Es gehe daher auch darum, Räume zu schaffen, in denen Lesen „zelebriert“ werde. Lesen sei „nicht nur eine wichtige Kompetenz, sondern etwas Schönes“.
Kleine Gruppen geben Sicherheit
Gearbeitet wird bei Startklar in kleinen Gruppen mit sechs bis acht Kindern. „Da trauen sich die Kinder auch mehr zu sprechen“, sagt Fischer. Gerade die Erfahrung, dass andere Kinder vor ähnlichen sprachlichen Herausforderungen stehen, gebe vielen zusätzliche Sicherheit.
Manche Kinder würden in den Gruppen erstmals Deutsch sprechen. Die Förderung beschränke sich dabei nicht nur auf die Sprache. Auch das soziale Verhalten der Kinder entwickle sich durch das Gruppensetting positiv, berichtet Fischer.
Mehrsprachigkeit als Bereicherung
Beim Umgang mit Mehrsprachigkeit sieht Fischer noch Aufholbedarf. Mehrsprachig aufwachsende Kinder würden häufig mit einsprachig aufwachsenden Kindern verglichen. Dabei könne die sprachliche Entwicklung mehr Zeit und gezielte Unterstützung benötigen.
Sommer-Fein ergänzt, dass Mehrsprachigkeit nicht als Nachteil betrachtet werden sollte. Sie sei „ein absolutes Geschenk und eine Bereicherung“. Wichtig sei, dass Kinder in ihren Sprachen eine möglichst hohe Kompetenz entwickeln. Auch die Familiensprache müsse dabei berücksichtigt werden.
Neben der Förderung der Kinder spiele deshalb auch die Unterstützung der Familien eine zentrale Rolle. Sprache werde bereits im Baby- und Kleinkindalter über das Umfeld gelernt. Gleichzeitig sei es eine gesellschaftliche Aufgabe, Familien mit mehrsprachig aufwachsenden Kindern entsprechend zu unterstützen.
Unterstützung für Bildungseinrichtungen
Auch bei Pädagoginnen und Pädagogen gebe es laut Fischer noch Nachholbedarf. Die zahlreichen Anfragen von Bildungseinrichtungen würden zeigen, dass der Bedarf an zusätzlicher Unterstützung groß sei. Es fehle teilweise an Wissen darüber, wie mehrsprachig aufwachsende Kinder gezielt gefördert werden können.
Die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Bildungseinrichtungen und außerschulischen Initiativen wie Startklar könne hier unterstützen, sagt Sommer-Fein. Der Verein könne gezielt an einzelnen Themen arbeiten und damit eine Ergänzung zur Arbeit in den Bildungseinrichtungen bieten.

title: Người phụ nữ để nẹp vít 4 năm trong chân, bác sĩ phải khoan phá để tháo
content:
Người phụ nữ để nẹp vít 4 năm trong chân, bác sĩ phải khoan phá để tháo
TP HCMGần 4 năm sau phẫu thuật gãy xương, người phụ nữ đến viện tháo nẹp vít nhưng can xương đã bám chặt, bác sĩ phải khoan phá để lấy dụng cụ.
Ngày 22/9, BS.CK2 Nguyễn Bảo Dũng, Quản lý điều hành Khoa Chấn thương Chỉnh hình, Bệnh viện Đa khoa Khu vực Hóc Môn, cho biết người bệnh từng phẫu thuật kết hợp xương vùng cẳng chân và cổ chân hai bên bằng đinh, nẹp vít. Sau gần 4 năm, chị đến viện với mong muốn tháo dụng cụ.
Thăm khám và X-quang cho thấy xương đã liền tốt, đủ điều kiện phẫu thuật. Tuy nhiên, khi mổ, bác sĩ phát hiện can xương phát triển bao phủ và bám chặt gần như toàn bộ đinh, nẹp, vít. Một số vít bị tuôn đầu khi vặn, khiến dụng cụ tháo vít thông thường không còn hiệu quả. Êkíp phải sử dụng màn hình tăng sáng C-arm để xác định vị trí dụng cụ trong quá trình phẫu thuật.
Bác sĩ bóc tách lớp can xương, dùng dụng cụ chuyên dụng khoan phá vùng mũ vít và quanh chân vít, từng bước lấy dụng cụ và hạn chế tổn thương xương lành. Sau phẫu thuật, toàn bộ đinh, nẹp, vít được lấy ra an toàn, không gây nứt hoặc gãy xương, người bệnh hồi phục tốt.
Theo bác sĩ Dũng, sau phẫu thuật gãy xương, nhiều người hết đau, đi lại bình thường nên không tái khám hoặc không biết khi nào cần kiểm tra, tháo dụng cụ. Thời điểm tháo phụ thuộc vào vị trí và mức độ gãy, loại dụng cụ, tình trạng liền xương, sức khỏe và nhu cầu của từng người.
Không phải tất cả trường hợp đều cần tháo đinh, nẹp, vít. Nếu có chỉ định nhưng để quá lâu, can xương có thể bao phủ dụng cụ, khiến phẫu thuật khó hơn; vít có thể bị kẹt, tuôn đầu, đinh hoặc nẹp khó lấy ra, tăng nguy cơ tổn thương xương lành, nứt hoặc gãy xương. Ngược lại, tháo quá sớm khi xương chưa liền vững có thể làm mất sự hỗ trợ cơ học tại ổ gãy, tăng nguy cơ di lệch, chậm liền, khớp giả hoặc gãy lại.
Một số đinh nhỏ như đinh Kirschner có thể được cân nhắc tháo sau khoảng 3-6 tháng; nẹp vít hoặc đinh nội tủy thường khoảng 1-2 năm. Đây chỉ là mốc tham khảo, không áp dụng cứng nhắc. Bác sĩ cần dựa vào thăm khám và X-quang để đánh giá mức độ liền xương trước khi quyết định.
Sau khi tháo dụng cụ, xương vẫn cần thời gian phục hồi. Các vị trí từng đặt vít còn để lại lỗ trên xương. Trong khoảng 2-3 tháng đầu, người bệnh nên hạn chế mang vác nặng, vận động mạnh, các môn thể thao đối kháng và tránh té ngã. Cần tái khám, chụp X-quang theo lịch để đánh giá quá trình hồi phục.
Người từng phẫu thuật kết hợp xương nên lưu giữ hồ sơ điều trị, biết loại dụng cụ đã được đặt và tái khám theo hẹn. Khi muốn tháo đinh, nẹp, vít, cần được bác sĩ chuyên khoa đánh giá thay vì tự quyết định dựa vào thời gian mang dụng cụ hoặc cảm giác hết đau.

title: Amid affordability crisis for artists, Vancouver’s city council establishes cultural land trust
content:
Supporters of a motion that was passed by Vancouver’s city council in July, greenlighting the creation of a cultural land trust (CLT), see it as a way to keep artists and art nonprofits in one of Canada’s most expensive cities—and an extension of a model other places have embraced to support their creative communities.
According to Brian McBay, the executive director of the local artist residency and cultural programming nonprofit 221a, more than 400,000 sq. ft of artists’ studios and other workspaces have been lost across Vancouver over the past decade. Since 2018, 221a has led research, feasibility analysis and sector consultation to find ways of keeping artists in the city and the wider province; it has found that over 80% of artists and cultural organisations in British Columbia face economic displacement.
The creation of a Vancouver CLT has been championed by McBay and others as a way to alleviate some of the pressures on the city’s creative class. After a motion to create the trust was introduced by city councillor Sean Orr, it was passed unanimously on 15 July.
Multi-step process
The CLT model involves a multi-step process, whereby funds and buildings received from government and philanthropic sources are financed, acquired or developed for cultural uses. Cultural nonprofit partners are engaged through long-term leases or equity ownership, removing properties from the speculative market. In turn, land trust assets are leveraged for additional growth, and the land trust becomes a core advocate for regulatory improvements and cultural sector learning.
“Rather than supporting one building at a time, [the CLT] creates a permanent capital platform that enables small- and medium-sized arts organisations to access ownership opportunities that would otherwise remain out of reach,” McBay said in a statement.
The framework adopted in Vancouver paves the way for partnerships with the municipal government and the creation of a portfolio of eligible city-owned buildings by March 2027. The motion was also amended to mandate that properties under consideration for the trust will primarily rely on long-term leases—a big issue in a city where many cultural spaces have short-term leases—to help ensure properties’ continued public ownership.
The CLT model has been adopted in many cities where real-estate prices routinely threaten the longevity of cultural spaces and artists’ livelihoods. These include London, where the Creative Land Trust was founded in 2020. Helsinki has had a version of a CLT, the organisation Kaapeli, since 1991; it now manages almost 100,000 sq. m of space across three properties that it leases for creative uses. The Bay Area, meanwhile, has two programmes in this vein: the Community Arts Stabilization Trust and the Artist Space Trust.
Rather than supporting one building at a time, the CLT creates a permanent capital platformBrian McBay, executive director, 221a
Adapted to Vancouver’s unique context, McBay says, a CLT could allow artists and arts organisations to focus on delivering cultural programming while the trust undertakes asset acquisition, long-term stewardship, capital planning and portfolio management. He sees it as a way of “de-commodifying ownership” by supporting artists and nonprofits to “acquire real estate, preventing displacement and securing affordability, but also using the power that comes with land ownership to reshape municipal redevelopment towards a less transactional city”.
First property secured
McBay’s efforts have already borne fruit thanks to the donation of a home on Vancouver’s West Side from the estate of the late scholar Evelyn Pinkerton, marking the CLT’s first asset. The 1920s-era wood-frame house requires C$250,000 ($178,000) worth of repairs and stabilisation work for safe occupancy and the long-term use envisioned by the trust and 221a—namely as community housing and residency spaces for artists.
McBay says the house will function as “proof of concept for funders and, crucially, as a financial asset that can be borrowed against to support other property-related acquisitions by the CLT”. He and his colleagues have set a goal of securing 30 buildings for long-term cultural programming and artists’ housing by 2050, and are seeking to raise C$15m ($10.7m) in seed funding.
Councillor Orr, whose days as a touring musician first alerted him to Vancouver’s vanishing cultural spaces, says it is still early days for the city’s CLT. Next, municipal staff will prepare a report, including a review of properties and funding requirements, to be presented to the council in the first quarter of 2027.

title: From roadside deliveries to safe births: Dadetoklo gets lifeline CHPS compound after years of health struggle
content:
Audio By Carbonatix
For years, the people of Dadetoklo, a quiet fishing village in the Sene East District of the Bono East Region, lived with a painful reality: bringing a child into the world often meant risking a mother's life.
The community's only hope for healthcare lay in Kojokrom, where the nearest CHPS compound is located. But the distance was only half the problem. The road leading there, dusty, riddled with potholes, and nearly impassable in the rainy season, turned every emergency into a desperate gamble.
Residents recall harrowing tales of pregnant women in labour being carried on motorbikes or bicycles, only to deliver midway through the journey. Some never made it at all.
"We have lost women on that road," a visibly emotional resident told JoyNews. "When labour starts at night, we panic. Sometimes the woman delivers in the bush. Sometimes, she bleeds and we can do nothing."
A Community's Cry
The story of Dadetoklo is one repeated across many rural communities in Ghana, where access to basic healthcare remains a daily battle. For the fishing families here, the river provides their livelihood but also isolates them from essential services.
Health workers in the area confirmed that the lack of a nearby facility contributed to preventable maternal deaths, delayed immunizations, and untreated illnesses.
Government Responds
That cry has finally been heard. The government, through the Sene East District Assembly, has constructed a modern CHPS compound for the community, a facility that now stands as a beacon of hope in the heart of the village.
The compound, complete with consulting rooms, a delivery ward, and accommodation for nurses, is expected to serve Dadetoklo and its surrounding settlements.
Residents who spoke to JoyNews could not hide their joy. "Now, when my daughter is pregnant, she will not suffer," said one elderly woman. "We thank the government. This is what we prayed for."
Regional Minister Commends Assembly
Bono East Regional Minister, Hon. Francis Owusu Antwi, who inspected the facility, lauded the District Assembly for prioritising the health and well-being of rural communities.
"This CHPS compound is not just a building; it is a promise kept," he said. "We cannot develop without a healthy population. Every woman in Dadetoklo deserves to deliver safely, and this facility will ensure that."
He urged residents to take full ownership of the facility and called on health authorities to ensure it is properly staffed and stocked.
A Step Forward, But Work Remains
While the new CHPS compound brings relief, residents say the road network connecting Dadetoklo to Kojokrom and beyond remains a pressing concern. They are appealing to the government to rehabilitate the road, which they say is critical not only for health emergencies but also for trade and daily movement.
For now, however, the community is celebrating a victory years in the making.
For the women of Dadetoklo, the days of praying through labour pains on a bumpy road may finally be over. A new chapter has begun one where a mother's life is no longer the price of distance.

title: Bác sĩ Chợ Rẫy phối hợp cứu 2 bệnh nhân nhồi máu cơ tim ngay tại đặc khu Phú Quốc
content:
Ngày 19-9, bác sĩ CK2 Lý Ích Trung - Trưởng khoa tim mạch can thiệp Bệnh viện Chợ Rẫy - cho biết bệnh viện vừa phối hợp Bệnh viện Mặt Trời Phú Quốc (An Giang) kịp thời can thiệp cấp cứu cho hai bệnh nhân nhồi máu cơ tim cấp và bán cấp tại đặc khu Phú Quốc.
Đây cũng là hai ca can thiệp tim mạch đầu tiên sau khi hai bệnh viện ký kết hợp tác chuyên môn vào tháng 7-2026.
Trường hợp thứ nhất là bệnh nhân L.V.Q. (65 tuổi) nhập viện lúc 0h ngày 14-9 do khó thở, mệt ở ngực, choáng váng, vã mồ hôi. Ngoài ra, ghi nhận bệnh nhân có tiền căn hút thuốc lá nhiều. Tại Bệnh viện Mặt Trời Phú Quốc, bệnh nhân được chẩn đoán nhồi máu cơ tim giờ thứ 3.
Ngay sau khi tiếp nhận thông tin, bác sĩ Nguyễn Tuấn Anh - khoa can thiệp tim mạch Bệnh viện Chợ Rẫy, nhân sự vừa được bệnh viện điều động đến Phú Quốc - đã nhanh chóng phối hợp ê kíp của Bệnh viện Mặt Trời Phú Quốc can thiệp cấp cứu cho bệnh nhân.
Bệnh nhân được tái thông thành công động mạch vành phải đoạn xa, phục hồi tốt dòng chảy. Sau thủ thuật, bệnh nhân giảm các triệu chứng tức ngực và khó thở, diễn tiến phục hồi tốt trên lâm sàng.
Đêm cùng ngày, Bệnh viện Mặt Trời Phú Quốc tiếp tục tiếp nhận bệnh nhân P.N.V. (58 tuổi). Bệnh nhân có tiền căn hút thuốc lá nhiều và hai tuần trước nhập viện có triệu chứng mệt ở ngực, khó thở kéo dài.
Cách nhập viện hai ngày, bệnh nhân đi khám sức khỏe và được ghi nhận kết quả điện tim bất thường nên kiểm tra chuyên sâu. Kết quả cận lâm sàng ghi nhận bệnh nhân bị giảm động vách liên thất vùng mỏm, giảm chức năng tâm thu thất trái...
Bệnh nhân được chẩn đoán nhồi máu cơ tim bán cấp thành trước, suy tim, rối loạn lipid máu, đái tháo đường typ 2. Bệnh nhân nhanh chóng được can thiệp, kết quả bệnh nhân đã được tái thông thành công, sức khỏe diễn tiến hồi phục tốt sau thủ thuật.
Theo bác sĩ CK2 Lý Ích Trung, cả hai bệnh nhân đều bị nhồi máu cơ tim có nguy cơ tử vong cao và cần được thực hiện can thiệp tái thông động mạch vành càng sớm càng tốt.
Ngược lại, trong tình huống không được xử lý tại Phú Quốc, bệnh nhân phải di chuyển đến các cơ sở y tế có phòng thông tim trong đất liền hoặc TP.HCM thời gian ước chừng khoảng vài giờ.
Mỗi giờ chậm trễ can thiệp có thể làm tăng nguy cơ tử vong cho bệnh nhân khoảng 5-10%.
Vì vậy, thời gian từ khi tiếp nhận đến khi can thiệp càng ngắn thì tỉ lệ vùng cơ tim hoại tử càng giảm, giúp giảm biến chứng cho người bệnh.

title: Trump cancelled a $7B solar energy grant program. A judge just ordered its revival
content:
More than a year after federal regulators abruptly canceled a $7 billion solar energy grant program — with funds already distributed and even partially spent — a Rhode Island federal judge has ordered them to revive the program.
But it’s too early for the group of union laborers, solar panel installation companies, homeowners, and nonprofit advocates who filed the complaint in October 2025 against the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to declare victory.
“The result is maddeningly difficult to talk about what happens next because we just don’t know what they’ll do,” said Kevin Hubbard, executive director of the Lawyers’ Committee for Rhode Island, one of the attorneys for the plaintiffs.
The 20-page order issued on Friday by U.S. Judge Mary S. McElroy of the U.S. District Court for Rhode Island determines that the federal agency overstepped its statutory authority when it ended the $7 billion Solar for All grant program in August 2025.
Originally included in the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act, the Biden-era incentive program sought to make solar panels more widely accessible by offsetting the installation costs for low-to-moderate-income homeowners and renters. Funding was distributed in 2024 to state and local governments, nonprofits, and tribal organizations, including a $49.3 million allocation to Rhode Island through the state’s Office of Energy Resources.
Many funding recipients, including Rhode Island, had already set up the framework to begin giving out the money to eligible applicants, with union laborers and solar development companies at the ready for an expected 200,000 jobs over the course of the five-year program.
The grants were expected to help $900,000 households nationwide save $350 million annually on their energy bills, according to prior estimates from the Biden administration.
“This will be a really big deal for solar deployment in Rhode Island,” said Patrick Crowley, president of the Rhode Island AFL-CIO, which was one of the plaintiffs in the suit. “This program could really be a game changer for meeting our Act on Climate goals.”
The 2021 decarbonization law requires the state to reach net-zero emissions by 2050, with incremental benchmarks starting in 2030. Based on the 9.52 million metric tons of net greenhouse gas emissions measured in 2023, Rhode Island would need more than 25,000 megawatts of solar, wind, and other renewable powered-electricity to reach net zero. Including the 400 megawatts from the nearly finished Revolution Wind project, the state has 1,418 megawatts of clean energy capacity, as of the second quarter of 2026.
The prospect of advancing Rhode Island’s renewable energy while boosting the local economy through the Solar for All program never materialized, almost immediately thrust into limbo when President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, and ended permanently by the EPA via a social media video published Aug. 7.
The AFL-CIO, accompanied by other nonprofit and business groups, sued in October 2025.
Federal environmental regulators pointed to the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” signed into law on July 4, which rescinded the congressional authority for the program and clawed back any unspent funds, as justification for the termination.
McElroy rejected this interpretation.
“Defendants’ preferred approach runs contrary to Congress’s clear intent that already obligated Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund monies, including SFA grants, not be disturbed by the repeal of Section 134,” she wrote. “They provide no legal authority for their proposition that the obligated SFA funds were somehow converted into lump-sum amounts untethered to the program for which they were originally appropriated.”
Although McElroy threw out the cancellation order, she didn’t specify how federal administrators should revive the solar grant program.
The “ideal” outcome, said Hubbard, would be that the federal agency allows the program to continue through the recipients already awarded grant funds. But, it could decide to start anew, forcing recipients to reapply for the competitive funding and delaying the entire process of putting more solar panels on rooftops.
Based on the Trump administration’s actions in almost every legal challenge it has encountered, Hubbard is expecting federal regulators will appeal McElroy’s order anyway.
An unidentified spokesperson for the EPA said the agency is “reviewing the decision and considering options for appeal.”
If and when the case is finalized and funds are released, Crowley said there are electricians, iron workers, and laborers ready to jump in on the jobs.
“We already have trained tradespeople to start doing this work,” he said, noting that renewable energy sector jobs have dried up since the change in presidential administrations.
There were more than 15,000 clean energy jobs in Rhode Island as of January 2025, according to an August report by Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources. The job count, which does not reflect any changes to the state economy since Trump took office, marked the highest industry employment in five years, buoyed by large increases in heating and cooling jobs thanks to a state rebate program for residential heat pumps. Wind and solar employment stayed relatively flat year over year, the report showed.
But the state needs clarity on the outcome of the Solar for All complaint before it can proceed with Rhode Island’s $49 million grant, Robert Beadle, a spokesperson for the Office of Energy Resources, said in an email.
Other plaintiffs in the lawsuit include the Rhode Island Center for Justice, which had increased its staff of public interest attorneys in preparation for the grant rollout; a Georgia homeowner who applied for free solar installation; and businesses and nonprofits that work on solar panel installation, financing, and education.
“Our low-income clients continue to face ever-escalating housing and utility costs, Jennifer L. Wood, executive director of the Rhode Island Center for Justice, said in a statement. “This is a major step toward restoring an important path to utility affordability for Rhode Islanders struggling to afford stable housing and access to utilities.”
The Southern Environmental Law Center, Lawyers for Good Government, and the Conservation Law Foundation also represented the plaintiffs.
This article was originally published by the Rhode Island Current.

title: From social media to Parliament: Barik beats bigger party machines to claim PUD’s lone seat
content: He did not have one of the election’s bigger party machines behind him. What Oussama Barik did have was a name built over years of talking online about broken roads, isolated mountain communities and the everyday grievances of Midelt.On Wednesday, that was enough to take him to Parliament.Oussama Barik, a young content creator better known by that name than his given name, Abdelaziz, topped the poll in his constituency with more than 32,000 votes, beating candidates from the Popular Movement and PAM on his way to the House of Representatives.The ticket he rode was an unlikely one. Barik stood for the Unity and Democracy Party (PUD), a small formation whose faucet symbol was considerably less familiar on the national political scene than the emblems of the parties he was up against.When the countrywide numbers were added up, PUD had won one of Parliament’s 395 seats. Midelt had delivered it.Barik’s win was years in the making, though not through the usual party route. His constituency had largely been online.Through videos shared on social media, he built an audience around problems that seldom need much explaining in Midelt’s mountain country; villages cut off or poorly connected, weak infrastructure and the struggle to reach basic services. Imilchil and other mountain areas regularly featured in his videos.It was local politics without much of the party wrapping, and Barik carried that name recognition into an election where he was facing candidates backed by far bigger organizations.The Popular Movement, long a player in rural and mountain constituencies, finished the national election with 29 seats. PAM topped the provisional national standings with 97. Neither label was enough to get past Barik in Midelt.The result also produced one of the election’s more unusual journeys to Parliament. Barik had not made his name climbing through a party hierarchy or holding national office. He arrived on voters’ phones, talking about the roads, services and isolation of communities around them.

title: President Mirziyoyev visits greenhouse project in Kegeyli district.
content:
Reportedly, the project received UZS 12.5 billion in concessional financing to build a modern greenhouse using lightweight structures on a five-hectare site. In its first stage, the project involved 50 families listed in the Social Register, providing them with permanent employment. Each participating family has 0.1 hectares of greenhouse space and receives training and practical support from the entrepreneur overseeing the project.
Over the next two years, participating families will receive hands-on training to develop the knowledge and skills needed to set up their own greenhouses on their household plots and build a stable source of income. The entrepreneur will also purchase the agricultural products they grow at market prices, the presidential press service said.
The greenhouse facility also trains up to 1,000 people each year in modern greenhouse and farming techniques, helping residents develop stable sources of income. Around 500 ducks are being raised in a 350-metre canal near the greenhouse facility, with each participating family receiving 10 breeding ducks imported from Brazil, along with guidance on raising them.
The project was presented as an initiative to promote entrepreneurship and create jobs in rural areas. The site also uses resource-efficient technologies, including solar panels with a total capacity of 100 kilowatts, which provide enough electricity to meet the greenhouse facility’s daily needs.

title: Après plus de 15 ans d’absence, le comité “Esca’fête” fait revivre la ducasse d’Escanaffles ces 25, 26 et 27 septembre
content:
Après plus de 15 ans d'absence, le comité "Esca'fête" fait revivre la ducasse d'Escanaffles ces 25, 26 et 27 septembre
Après quinze ans d'absence, la ducasse fera son grand retour à Escanaffles, ce week-end. Durant trois jours, du vendredi 25 au dimanche 27 septembre, le village cellois renouera avec ses anciennes traditions festives à travers un programme entièrement gratuit.
- Publié le 21-09-2026 à 17h01
La nostalgie des ducasses de village… Quinze ans que les Escanafflois attendaient de pouvoir revivre ces moments festifs et conviviaux. Ce week-end, leur ducasse fera enfin son grand retour, avec trois jours de festivités entièrement gratuites.
"La ducasse occupait autrefois une place importante dans la vie locale, relève le comité Esca'Fêtes. Escanaffles en accueillait même trois chaque année, deux en juillet et l'autre en septembre."
Ducasse des Trentenaires, ducasse du Joncquois ou encore foire artisanale : autant de rendez-vous qui ont marqué la mémoire des habitants, et évoquent de nombreux souvenirs aux participants de ces festivités d'antan…
Depuis 2010, pourtant, plus aucune ducasse n'était organisée dans le village de l'entité de Celles. La disparition récente du club de football local a également marqué un tournant dans la vie associative d'Escanaffles. Mais certains anciens membres ont souhaité poursuivre leur engagement autrement.
"Une grande partie des personnes qui faisaient vivre le club ont souhaité continuer à animer leur village autrement. L'idée de recréer une grande fête populaire au cœur d'Escanaffles s'est rapidement imposée comme la meilleure façon de prolonger cette dynamique", explique le comité, qui a ainsi vu le jour sous le nom d'Esca'Fêtes.
L'objectif est de faire de cette nouvelle ducasse un rendez-vous porté par l'ensemble du village. "Elle doit devenir la ducasse de tous les Escanafflois. Notre volonté est de fédérer les habitants, les associations, l'école, les commerçants et les bénévoles autour d'un événement commun."
Les festivités débuteront ce vendredi 25 septembre à 18 h, avec un afterwork et une exposition de photographies anciennes du village, réalisée par les élèves de l'école communale. La soirée se poursuivra avec DJ Alex.
Samedi après-midi, place au FestiKids, avec de nombreuses activités pour les enfants : châteaux gonflables, grimage, jeux anciens. Après un repas "cochon à la broche", le groupe "À peu près ça" se produira à partir de 21 h pour un concert mêlant rock et humour.
La marche ADEPS (5, 10, 15 et 20 km) de l'école communale lancera les festivités du dimanche 27 septembre. À 11 h, le groupe "Dans Ton Cuivre" animera l'apéritif musical. À partir de 14 h, le traditionnel jeu de bourle fera son retour autour du village.

title: Malaysia's busiest airport cuts ride-hailing pickup fee to 49 cents at both terminals
content:
The new rate, inclusive of tax, replaces charges of RM3 at Terminal 1 and RM2.16 at Terminal 2 starting from last week, Bernama reported.
T1 serves full-service and medium-service carriers like Malaysia Airlines, Emirates, Singapore Airlines, and Qatar Airways, while T2, located two kilometers away, serves low-cost carriers like AirAsia and Scoot.
Airport operator Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said the change would give passengers and drivers one consistent fee.
MAHB introduced the Terminal 1 charge on Aug. 4 to fund the operation and maintenance of an upgraded pickup area, The Star reported.
The overhaul added a license plate recognition system, indoor waiting lounges and on-ground marshals.
Within a month, 99.3% of e-hailing drivers were completing pickups and leaving within the 10-minute grace period, up from 49.4%, the New Straits Times reported, citing MAHB.
The number of vehicles entering the pickup lanes daily fell 13.5% to 7,024, which the operator attributed to less unauthorized activity and idling.
Peak-hour capacity rose from 302 to as many as 660 vehicles an hour.
KLIA, Malaysia's busiest airport, handled 63.3 million passengers in 2025, up 10.8% from a year earlier, according to MAHB data.

title: Les maisons de transition sont des sas très efficaces entre la prison et la liberté, mais il n’en existe qu’une en Wallonie, pour 15 détenus…
content:
Les maisons de transition sont des sas très efficaces entre la prison et la liberté, mais il n'en existe qu'une en Wallonie, pour 15 détenus…
Le projet-pilote testé à Malines s'est étendu. Mais le nombre total de places (77) reste très modeste au regard des besoins. Du côté francophone, la maison de transition d'Enghien est la seule structure pour les détenus en fin de peine.
- Publié le 24-09-2026 à 18h50
Après la prison, comment reprendre pied dans la société libre ? Au terme de plusieurs années passées à l'ombre, comment rebondir à l'extérieur où tout a changé ? Une première maison de transition, conçue pour accompagner les futurs ex-détenus et faciliter leur réintégration, voyait le jour en 2019 à Malines.
Dans ce projet-pilote de détention à petite échelle, quinze détenus condamnés à de longues peines bénéficient, à partir de 18 mois avant la fin de leur peine, d'un accompagnement intensif pour reprendre progressivement leurs responsabilités, trouver un emploi, reconstruire un réseau social et préparer leur retour dans la société. Objectif final : prévenir la récidive et donc renforcer la sécurité.
Neuf résidents sur dix travaillent
Depuis la création de la maison de transition à Malines, environ 200 personnes sont passées par ce sas entre la prison et la liberté. Et ça marche. Neuf résidents sur dix travaillent pendant leur séjour. Plus de 120 résidents ont accédé à un plan de réinsertion solide. Deux périodes d'évaluation consécutives de trois ans se sont révélées positives, se félicitait mercredi la ministre de la Justice, Annelies Verlinden (CD & V) en inaugurant le nouveau site de la maison de transition de Malines. "Une exécution des peines réussie ne s'arrête pas aux portes de la prison. Elle n'est vraiment réussie que lorsqu'une personne, après avoir purgé sa peine, retrouve sa place dans la société sans faire de nouvelles victimes. C'est précisément pour cette raison que nous continuons à investir dans les maisons de transition", indique-t-elle.
Cinq nouvelles maisons en prévision
Le modèle s'est étendu. Après Malines, quatre autres maisons de transition ont vu le jour en Belgique, à Gentbrugge, Louvain, Enghien (la seule du côté francophone) et Hamme. Le nombre total actuel de places en maisons de transition (77) reste pourtant très modeste au regard des besoins : il y a plus de 13 500 détenus… "Tout le monde trouve que c'est un bon concept, mais nous sommes tout de même confrontés à de nombreux obstacles quand nous voulons développer ces projets", regrette mercredi Mathilde Steenbergen, directrice générale des établissements pénitentiaires.
Le gouvernement fédéral prévoit de dégager les moyens nécessaires à la création de cinq maisons de transition supplémentaires d'ici deux ans, dit la ministre Verlinden. Elles sont notamment envisagées à Anvers, Charleroi et Alken.
Parallèlement, l'arrêté royal fixant les normes applicables à ces maisons de détention à petite échelle a été modifié : leur capacité d'accueil passe de 12-17 résidents à 15-25 résidents pour les nouveaux projets. Ce qui permettra d'utiliser au mieux les moyens disponibles et d'accueillir davantage de résidents.

title: SPO disengaged over ‘fake’ records, Jammu and Kashmir High Court orders reinstatement
content:
4 min readNew DelhiSep 24, 2026 03:30 PM IST

The Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court has quashed the disengagement of a special police officer (SPO) accused of furnishing fake documents to conceal his age, holding that he was removed without a show-cause notice or inquiry.
Dealing with the SPO’s plea, Justice M A Chowdhary said the action violated natural justice and ordered his reinstatement, along with related benefits.
“The irrefutable conclusion that could be drawn is that the respondents indeed have violated the basic fundamental principle of natural justice, while ordering disengagement of the services of the Petitioner as SPO, thereby condemning him unheard,” the ruling observed.




The court added that the respondents proceeded against the petitioner, raising a seriou accusation, for which he was required to be heard in his defence.
SPOs denied constable conversion
The petitioner claimed to have been engaged as an SPO in the department in 2004. In 2007, the department started a process for the conversion of SPOs to constables on compassionate grounds. According to the petitioner, he, along with five other SPOs, was not considered for conversion to constables despite recommendations by the competent authority.
Justice M A Chowdhary observed that the petitioner was disengaged from service without issuing a show-cause notice or conducting an inquiry.
In 2011, the petitioner and the five other SPOs approached the high court which directed the authorities in 2012 to consider their appointment and absorption as constable drivers. The direction was upheld by a division bench in 2013.
While facing contempt proceedings, the authorities in May 2022 absorbed him and nine other SPOs as constables. He later noticed that his date of birth had been incorrectly recorded as March 4, 1981, instead of January 1, 1973. Although he informed the police authorities about the error, the correction was not made.
Story continues below this ad
Instead, the senior superintendent of police (security), Kashmir, passed an order on December 21, 2023, disengaging him from service. The authorities alleged that he had used fake and fabricated documents to conceal his actual age at the time of his SPO engagement and that he was over the prescribed age limit.
The petitioner challenged the disengagement before the high court, contending that the authorities had removed him without issuing a show-cause notice or conducting an inquiry.
Representing the state, Additional Advocate General Mohsin-ul-Showkat Qadri argued that the petitioner wilfully produced fake and fabricated documents to suppress his actual age with an ill design.
No prior notice: Order
The court observed that the respondents disengaged the petitioner without issuing a show-cause notice or conducting an inquiry prior to taking adverse action. The basic legal requirement that no person should be condemned unheard was completely ignored.
Story continues below this ad
The court noted that terminating or disengaging an employee based on serious, stigmatic allegations (such as submitting fake/fabricated documents) requires providing the individual with notice and a reasonable opportunity to present their defence before any punishment is imposed.
“From the perusal of the relevant record made available before this court by the respondents, nothing is forthcoming as to fact that the respondents have issued any prior notice to the petitioner or conducted any enquiry before disengaging the services of the petitioner,” the order said.
It emphasised that the petitioner was entitled to be afforded an opportunity of hearing before inflicting the major punishment of disengagement from service.

title: Au Festival du « Monde » : ces « maisons » pluridisciplinaires qui accompagnent les femmes victimes de violences
content:
Pour se reconstruire après avoir subi des violences sexuelles, encore faut-il pouvoir parler. « On vient lutter contre cette arme fatale qu’est le silence », explique la gynécologue obstétricienne Ghada Hatem-Gantzer. En 2016, elle ouvrait à Saint-Denis (Seine-Saint-Denis) la première Maison des femmes. Dix ans plus tard, le modèle s’est développé partout en France, avec une même ambition : ne plus laisser les victimes seules face aux conséquences des violences.
Devenues un point de repère pour les femmes victimes de violences, ces structures d’accueil, qui sont une trentaine en France à présent, réunissent prises en charge médicale, psychologique, sociale et juridique. L’objectif est d’éviter aux victimes de multiplier les interlocuteurs et de construire un parcours de soutien dans la durée. Et de permettre parfois, simplement de s’asseoir. « Le fait d’avoir un lieu dédié, cela change tout dans la prise en charge de ces femmes », raconte Ghada Hatem-Gantzer.
A Nancy, le dispositif d’accompagnement des victimes, dont 10 à 15 % sont des hommes, va plus loin. Au sein de la Maison de la résilience, créée en 2024 par Coraline Hingray, les patients bénéficient d’une prise en charge d’une durée moyenne de neuf mois afin de traiter toutes les dimensions du syndrome post-traumatique : de la thérapie jusqu’à l’accompagnement social et juridique.

title: Naturalist adventure in Victoria's east draws new wave of twitchers
content:
East Gippsland attracts new wave of twitchers, nature lovers, poets, artists and dreamers
A new wave of birdwatchers, nature lovers, poets, artists and dreamers are finding catharsis and connection in the Australian bush along the east coast of Victoria thanks to a new art and nature experience.
The Far East Flaneur is a six-day, five-night art and nature trail, that explores the 100-kilometre journey from Lake Tyers to Cape Conran in East Gippsland, and the little-known places of interest in between.
A pilot event was held in March and the organisers, local community arts collective FLOAT, are planning to hold the next edition in October.
Participants walked, kayaked and cycled through the tributaries of Lake Tyers and the East Gippsland Rail Trail before heading to Orbost and Marlo, where the Snowy River meets the sea, and onto Cape Conran.
Local artist Anli Vuong, who baked cookies, treats and vegan mooncakes as snacks for the journey, said the Flaneur was an opportunity to discover the creativity available in the community and become inspired by other people's passions.
"Younger generations are so locked into technology, we work on our phones, we relax on our phones, we watch movies on our phones," Ms Vuong said.
"I think there's a yearning to find that dopamine hit from being with other people in nature.
"We know that it's good for us."
Guided through secluded back ways, the group discovered birds, bugs, creatures and plant life along the way, encountering geologists, historians, Indigenous artists and poets who shared their knowledge and passion for the local area.
"You don't know what each day will bring," she said.
"You go for a walk, but you also might come across someone doing weaving or an artistic talent and they actually immerse you in their craft, which brings extra layers of depth and meaning to the walk."
Travellers camp in tents and cabins, with ample opportunity to go to the beach, sketch birds, record sounds, explore the bush and have slow conversations with others on the trail.
Communal meals feature locally grown and prepared artisan food shared around campfires and long tables.
"It's marketed as slow travel so if you want to race through it, this may not be the tour for you,"project manager Liz Filmer said.
"But you might be surprised how much you love it."
The event was designed to help re-energise East Gippsland's economy after a decade of drought, fires, COVID, and the end of the region's commercial timber and fishing industries.
The new twitchers
Tasmania-based poet and storyteller Bert Spinks, who joined the March Flaneur, guided the group's nature journalling and encouraged participants to observe the symphony of nature through a mindful looking glass.
Whether it was observing the ripples and currents of the lake water, the veins of thirsty gum leaves or understanding the habits and social hierarchies of the kingfishers, Mr Spinks said there was much to experience.
"East Gippsland is such an amazing place for encountering different bird species," he said.
He said birdwatching was a goal-driven activity that got people outdoors and forced them to pay attention, sensing birds with their eyes and ears and watching scenarios play out so they could tick them off their lists.
"It can be a bit of a soap opera or a royal rumble, especially this time of year, a lot of birds are competing over territory, their nesting and they want to have a secure zone for their children to grow up, so you see a lot of combat between different types of birds at this time of year," he said.
In a similar way that the naturalist art and literature movement of the late 19th century observed nature through a more scientific lens, Mr Spinks described the younger generation's curiosity with nature as more existential than romantic.
"I think we are realising that we don't have the connection with the world around us and we're likely to lose so much of nature in our lifetimes, so there is a sense of it would be nice to know what is out there, before it's all gone," he said.
Writing about the patterns of insects in the changing seasons, such as the presence of butterflies as the weather warms, he said grounding and immersing oneself in nature was an antidote to the anxieties of the modern world.
"These experiences help us unchain ourselves from all of the demands and dramas of the world that we live in,"Mr Spinks said.
"It's about disconnecting from all the unnecessary complications that are now accepted as part of the normal human experience."

title: Number of migrants arriving in Europe falls by 39 percent
content:
The number of migrants arriving in Europe by sea has fallen sharply, but the number of people dying or going missing continues to rise, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reported.
Since the beginning of 2026, around 60,000 migrants and refugees have arrived in Europe by sea, 39 percent fewer than last year.
The UN says the main sea routes to Europe remain among the world’s deadliest migration routes.
According to the IOM, at least 2,300 people have died or gone missing, compared with 2,000 during the same period last year.
The number of arrivals fell most sharply on the central Mediterranean route to Italy, by 55 percent to 21,400. At the same time, the number of deaths on the route increased from 844 to 996.
A total of 20,400 people arrived in Greece, while the number of deaths on the eastern Mediterranean route rose from 284 to 417. Spain, meanwhile, received 16,800 migrants arriving via the Atlantic and western Mediterranean routes. A total of 879 people died or went missing on those routes.
Experts believe the actual death toll is likely to be significantly higher, as many shipwrecks and disappearances go unreported.
Meanwhile, from January to mid-September, more than 17,000 migrants were intercepted at sea and returned to Libya.
The IOM is calling for stronger international cooperation, efforts to combat human trafficking and exploitation, and expanded safe and legal migration pathways.

title: Manal bounces back after failing to make it to u-19 WC team
content:
Manal Chauhan started playing cricket for a simple reason — he wanted to bunk school.
He would tell his parents he was going to school and head off to play cricket instead. “At that time, I was not that interested in the sport, but I kept playing,” Manal told The Hindu ahead of Monday’s second youth ODI between India under-19 and the Australian colts here.
“Gradually, I realised that there were age-group divisions and that you move forward through them and then play for the State. I became very interested in it, so I started giving it my full time.”
The boy from Morena has since led Madhya Pradesh to its maiden Cooch Behar Trophy title and made his India u-19 debut on the Sri Lanka tour, scoring 150 and an unbeaten 51 in the second youth Test.
But it wasn’t a smooth ride. After a decent Vinoo Mankad Trophy campaign, the all-rounder missed out on the u-19 World Cup. “I was very demotivated because I wanted to play the World Cup. At that time, I did not know that there would be further bilateral series like this,” he said.
His parents and coaches told him there would be more opportunities. “I thought that, at least, I would win the red-ball tournament for MP. I did not know that I would come this far from there.”
Madhya Pradesh did win the Cooch Behar Trophy. Then came the India call-up.
“The biggest learning has been that things will keep going up and down in life, but you have to stick to your work ethic,” he said.
Chandrakant Pandit has helped him work on the mental side of the game, while India u-19 coach Yere Goud taught him to forget mistakes and move on.
Manal is doing just that, taking it one step at a time.
